rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation is on line 63 in `tanh_activation_kernel_half`, which is ONLY invoked when `scalar_t` is `at::Half` (float16). The fixed input specification requires `dtype=torch.float32`. For float32 inputs, `AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND_HALF` dispatches to `tanh_activation_kernel_vectorized<float>`, never to the mutated `tanh_activation_kernel_half`. The dispatch logic: `if constexpr (std::is_same<scalar_t, at::Half>::value)` evaluates to false for float, so the mutated kernel is never called.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes `threadIdx.x` to `threadIdx.y` in the half-precision (fp16) kernel. However, the input specification fixes the dtype at `torch.float32`. The AT_DISPATCH macro dispatches float32 inputs to `tanh_activation_kernel_vectorized<float>`, which is NOT mutated. The `tanh_activation_kernel_half` containing the mutation is only invoked for `at::Half` dtype inputs. Since dtype is part of the fixed specification and cannot be changed under the testing contract, the mutated code path is never executed. This is a classic case of dead code under the fixed configuration - the mutation exists but cannot affect program behavior for the specified inputs.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract (dtype=float32). To kill it would require changing the input dtype to float16/torch.half, which would violate the contract. If float16 were allowed, the mutation would cause catastrophic failure: with 1D blocks (blockDim.y=1), threadIdx.y is always 0, so all 512 threads per block would write to the same output index, leaving 99.95% of elements uninitialized garbage.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing CUDA kernels with dtype-dispatched paths, ensure the test contract allows testing all dtype branches. Consider adding dtype as a variable dimension in the testing contract, or create separate mutant-testing configurations for each dispatched dtype. The current fixed-dtype contract creates unreachable code paths in multi-dtype kernels.
